answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding each agent to escrowed stake and verifiable computation. Every staked agent is a vertex in a work graph, and rewards flow only along edges peers attested. A sybil attacker fabricating a hundred identities must escrow a hundred deposits and run compute per vertex, so flooding costs more than the payouts it could steal. Payment is tied to proven work: an agent paid to model how a river floods or compose a sonnet must attach signed proof from its staked identity, and unattested output earns nothing. Impostors drain their own collateral.
